newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end at record on foreign bids.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end at record on foreign bids.

text.p: Caracas stocks regained their footing after dipping earlier this week, rising in heavy trade on strong foreign and local bids, traders said.
"The bolsa's looking very good ... there are foreign investors supporting the trend, which I think is here to stay," said Intervalores broker Ricardo Marino.
The 19-share index jumped 1.23 percent to end at 7,345.57 points as 132 million shares traded worth 12 billion bolivars ($26 million), according to preliminary figures from the exchange.
"It's been very busy, very animated .. Just look at Electricidad de Caracas, 13 million shares traded, that gives you an idea," Cavelba trader Harold Cuellar said.
Electricidad closed up 2.14 percent at 572.00 bolivars.
But it was Corimon B shares that led trade volume, at over 60 million shares. The stock closed off 1.47 percent at 16.75 bolivars.
"There are a lot of rumors, some say there's a foreign investor that wants to buy the company ... but to me it looks expensive," said one broker.
